name: Rama
role: Exiled prince and hero-king of the Ramakien, an avatar of Vishnu
fun_fact: In the Ramakien he is Phra Ram, an avatar of the god Narai, and the kings of Thailand's Chakri dynasty took the name Rama.

name: Sita
role: Wife of Rama, abducted by Thotsakan and rescued after the war
fun_fact: In the Ramakien she is Nang Sida, also called Phra Laksami, which links her to the goddess Lakshmi, consort of Vishnu.

name: Ravana
role: Ten-necked demon king of Longka who abducts Sita
fun_fact: His Thai name Thotsakan means 'ten-necked', and the Ramakien shows him with ten faces and twenty arms.

name: Hanuman
role: White monkey warrior, son of the wind god and devoted servant of Rama
fun_fact: In the Ramakien he is a cheerful womanizer as well as a hero, and he fathers a son with the mermaid Suphanamatcha.

name: Lakshmana
role: Rama's younger brother and loyal companion in exile and war
fun_fact: In the Ramakien, Phra Lak is struck down by Intharachit's arrow, and his wound sends Hanuman to fetch the healing mountain.

name: Dewi Sri
role: Rice goddess of Java and Bali, also called Nyai Pohaci Sanghyang Asri
fun_fact: Rice is said to grow from her navel, and Balinese farmers still keep small shrines for her in the fields and granaries.

name: Naga
role: Serpent guardian of rivers, relics and the Buddhist teaching, honoured as Phaya Naga on the Mekong
fun_fact: At the end of Buddhist Lent, crowds on the Mekong watch for the Naga fireballs, which many believers read as the naga's celebration.

name: Kinnari
role: Bird-woman of Southeast Asian Buddhist and courtly art, the female counterpart of the kinnara
fun_fact: The female is a kinnari and the male a kinnara; in Thai art they often hold musical instruments and dance.

name: Manohara
role: Kinnari heroine captured by a hunter and wooed by Prince Suthon
fun_fact: Her tale is performed as Nora dance-drama in southern Thailand, and reliefs at Borobudur in Java are linked to an early version.

name: Mucalinda
role: Naga king who shelters the meditating Buddha from a great storm
fun_fact: The naga-prok image of the Buddha under a naga hood, common in Thailand and Cambodia, recalls his shelter.
